section_summary: This section documents the coordination, policy debates, and diplomatic preparations between the Department of State and the Department of the Army regarding SWNCC/SANACC 384 on the economic recovery of Japan. It details State Department efforts to ensure that proposals to assist Japanese economic self-support through congressional appropriations and trade expansion comply with Far Eastern Commission policies and do not prematurely dismantle occupation reforms or alienate Asian allies. The documents also reflect international reactions to U.S. recovery policy, including Soviet press condemnations of American economic plans and Chinese editorial opposition to the revival of Japanese industrial dominance.

subfiles.about: Outlines the clearance schedule and inter-departmental negotiations between the State Department and the Army over the redraft of SANACC 384.
subfiles.summary: Claxton reports clearances on the redraft of SANACC 384, Army coordination with Draper, and contingency plans for General McCoy's statement to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.title: Back-up Material for Mr. Saltzman

subfiles.about: Recommends obtaining Under Secretary Draper's agreement on a diplomatic courtesy statement for General McCoy to read to the Far Eastern Commission concerning congressional appropriation requests.
subfiles.summary: Claxton recommends clearing with Draper a statement informing the Far Eastern Commission of planned congressional requests for Japanese rehabilitation funds as a diplomatic courtesy.
subfiles.title: Clearance with Mr. Draper of Memorandum for General McCoy to Read Before FEC Regarding Intention to Request Congress for Funds for Japanese Rehabilitation

subfiles.about: Transmits a draft statement for General McCoy to deliver informally before the Far Eastern Commission regarding forthcoming U.S. appropriation requests for Japanese self-support.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman provides General McCoy with an advance draft statement informing the Far Eastern Commission that the Army will request congressional appropriations for Japanese economic self-support.
subfiles.title: Draft Letter to General Frank R. McCoy with Enclosed Draft Statement for the Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Transmits the formal text of an informal announcement for General McCoy to make to the Far Eastern Commission concerning congressional requests for Japanese economic assistance.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman forwards the approved statement for General McCoy to deliver to the Far Eastern Commission, announcing forthcoming requests to Congress for fiscal year 1949 recovery funds.
subfiles.title: Letter to General Frank R. McCoy Transmitting Statement for the Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Sets forth the Department of State's reasons for disapproving the Army proposal SANACC 384/1 on Japanese economic recovery.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman explains State Department objections to SANACC 384/1, arguing that granting SCAP a vague shift of emphasis would undermine Washington policy control and provoke severe Allied opposition in the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.title: The Economic Recovery of Japan - SANACC 384/1

subfiles.about: Submits State Department proposals and a draft policy resolution for the Far Eastern Commission to accelerate Japanese economic recovery through international cooperation.
subfiles.summary: State Member Charles E. Saltzman presents SANACC 384/2 as a constructive alternative to the Army's recovery proposals, emphasizing that Japanese economic self-support requires international cooperation and raw material access rather than unilateral U.S. directives. The memorandum warns that bypassing the Far Eastern Commission or reversing agreed occupation reforms would jeopardize Allied support and destabilize Japan. It includes a comprehensive draft statement and resolution for General McCoy to submit to the Commission, calling for the removal of entry restrictions on Allied businessmen, travel permission for Japanese traders, and trade planning beyond mere disease and unrest standards.
subfiles.title: SANACC 384/2: Economic Recovery of Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits a cleared draft revision of the SANACC 384 statement on Japanese economic recovery for coordination with the Army.
subfiles.summary: Claxton forwards a cleared redraft of the SANACC 384 statement for presentation to the Army, emphasizing Japanese self-support, Allied cooperation, and planned congressional requests for industrial raw material imports.
subfiles.title: Draft Revision of SANACC 384 Series for Presentation to the Army

subfiles.about: Submits the Department of the Army's proposal to expedite Japanese economic recovery, determine reparations, and issue a directive authorizing SCAP to shift occupation emphasis.
subfiles.summary: Under Secretary of the Army William H. Draper, Jr. presents SANACC 384/1, urging that the occupation enter a new phase focused on creating a self-sustaining Japanese economy to end the financial burden on American taxpayers. The paper recommends that SANACC approve a resolution for introduction into the Far Eastern Commission and dispatch a direct policy directive to General MacArthur instructing him to implement a shift of emphasis favoring economic revival. It includes a draft FEC resolution and a U.S. policy statement calling for the rapid determination of reparations and industrial levels to encourage Japanese self-support.
subfiles.title: SANACC 384/1: The Economic Recovery of Japan

subfiles.about: Communicates the State Department's views and counter-draft on Japanese economic recovery in response to the Army's revision of SANACC 384.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman responds to Draper's revision of SANACC 384, agreeing on the necessity of Japanese economic recovery but stressing that policy statements must not imply a repudiation of basic occupation reforms. He transmits a State Department redraft formulated as a formal statement and resolution for General McCoy to deliver before the Far Eastern Commission. The enclosed statement urges Allied cooperation to expand trade beyond minimum relief levels and recommends removing travel restrictions on businessmen entering and leaving Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter to William H. Draper, Jr., Transmitting State Department Counter-Draft of SANACC 384

subfiles.about: Expresses approval of the OE draft memorandum on SWNCC 384 and suggests amendments regarding SCAP directives and FEC authority.
subfiles.summary: Borton approves the draft memorandum opposing SWNCC 384 and suggests amendments regarding SCAP's authority, interim directives, and the impropriety of reiterating past directives.
subfiles.title: SWNCC 384

subfiles.about: Recommends editorial changes to the State Department draft memorandum concerning SWNCC 384.
subfiles.summary: Fearey concurs with the draft memorandum on SWNCC 384 and proposes specific editorial revisions regarding inter-departmental discussions and SWNCC 381.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on SWNCC 384

subfiles.about: Details the State Department's formal objections to the Army's proposal SWNCC 384 on Japanese economic recovery.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman rejects SWNCC 384, arguing that SWNCC 381 already provides a comprehensive recovery program, that unilateral directives alienate Asian allies, and that established level-of-industry agreements in SWNCC 236/43 must not be reopened.
subfiles.title: The Economic Recovery of Japan - SWNCC 384

subfiles.about: Announces the informal approval of amended SWNCC 384 and transmits copies for State Department implementation.
subfiles.summary: Transmits approved copies of amended SWNCC 384, noting agreements for FEC presentation, publication, and transmission to SCAP.
subfiles.title: SWNCC 384

subfiles.about: Instructs holders of SWNCC 384 to downgrade their copies from Secret to Unclassified.
subfiles.summary: Requests holders of SWNCC 384 to downgrade their copies from Secret to Unclassified.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for Holders of SWNCC 384: The Economic Recovery of Japan

subfiles.about: Records the informal approval of amended SWNCC 384, directs page substitutions, and terminates action on SANACC 384/1.
subfiles.summary: Records approval of amended SWNCC 384, orders substitution of revised pages, and terminates action on SANACC 384/1.
subfiles.title: Decision Amending SWNCC 384: The Economic Recovery of Japan

subfiles.about: Circulates the Army Member's memorandum and draft policy statement urging accelerated Japanese economic recovery and reduced U.S. relief costs.
subfiles.summary: SWNCC circulates an Army proposal stating that the initial phase of the occupation is complete and that prompt measures must be taken to create a self-sustaining Japanese economy. The document stresses the need to determine reparations quickly and to issue a directive instructing SCAP to foster economic recovery in order to relieve American taxpayers of relief burdens. The enclosed policy statement, revised for presentation to the Far Eastern Commission and transmission to SCAP, emphasizes peaceful industrial expansion and announces planned congressional funding requests for fiscal year 1949.
subfiles.title: SWNCC 384: The Economic Recovery of Japan

subfiles.about: Reviews Far Eastern Commission precedents regarding whether a national delegation may unilaterally withdraw a proposal after formal submission.
subfiles.summary: Pfuntner analyzes FEC precedents, concluding that a delegation cannot withdraw an introduced proposal unilaterally without formal leave from the considering body.
subfiles.title: Withdrawal of Proposals

subfiles.about: Inquires about U.S. policies and economic projections regarding Japanese industrialization, population, productivity, foreign investment, and trade.
subfiles.summary: Hirsch submits ten detailed questions to the State Department regarding Japanese de-industrialization, projected 1950 labor productivity, foreign investment opportunities, and international trade prospects.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Regarding Japanese Economic Prospects

subfiles.about: Responds to Donald B. Hirsch's inquiries regarding Japanese economic recovery, labor force estimates, exchange controls, and occupation publications.
keywords: Division of Occupied Areas Economic Affairs
subfiles.summary: Whitman answers Hirsch's questions regarding Japanese economic recovery, estimating 1950 labor force percentages, discussing foreign investment and exchange controls, and enclosing official occupation publications.
subfiles.title: Reply to Donald B. Hirsch Concerning Japanese Economic Policies

subfiles.about: Transmits and analyzes Soviet press articles from Trud and Izvestiya attacking United States economic recovery policies in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The American Embassy in Moscow reports on Soviet press commentary criticizing U.S. economic policy in Japan, enclosing a translation of M. Markov's article from Trud and reviewing an Izvestiya editorial attacking Secretary of War Kenneth Royall. The Soviet articles accuse the United States of halting demilitarization, preserving Japanese monopolies, and converting Japan into an American industrial and military bastion in the Far East. The commentary further alleges that Wall Street seeks to establish an American-Japanese economic cartel while delaying reparations and subordinating Asian markets.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 121: Soviet Press Articles Condemning US Economic Policy in Japan

subfiles.about: Reports on a Shanghai Ta Kung Pao editorial strongly opposing U.S. plans to rehabilitate the Japanese economy.
subfiles.summary: Cabot summarizes a Ta Kung Pao editorial condemning U.S. proposals to rehabilitate Japanese industry, charging that the policy revives Japanese domination of Asia and alienates China.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 202 from Shanghai Regarding Chinese Opposition to Japanese Economic Rehabilitation

subfiles.about: Informs Charles E. Saltzman of Robert A. Lovett's view that FEC 230 should be withdrawn and notes internal State Department discussions.
subfiles.summary: Claxton advises Saltzman that Lovett favors withdrawing FEC 230, noting planned coordination with Thorp, Allison, and Butterworth.
subfiles.title: Note Regarding the Withdrawal of FEC 230
